solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gossip about mad character having fight

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the Mad Hatter is the character from Alice in Wonderland
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A rumour-monger discussing a lunatic who gets into a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is a person who talks incessantly, which is exactly what a chatterbox is.

clue.text: Company regularly commandeering best horses

indicators.note: commandeering means the first piece seizes and takes on the second
regularly means taking every other letter of the word best

explanation.surface: A firm requisitioning the finest horses on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobs are sturdy, short-legged riding horses, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Article Independent journalist turned over to assistant

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: turned over means the journalist's letters are flipped to read upwards in this down light

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper article by an independent reporter handed over to an assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to someone in an official post.

clue.text: Military fiasco in Egypt has FBI worried about nothing

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
worried suggests the letters of Egypt has FBI being agitated into a new order

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: American agents fret over nothing in Egypt, while a military disaster unfolds.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion of Cuba by CIA-backed exiles was a notorious military failure.

clue.text: Sovereign leader finally united the French Resistance

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of leader

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
le is French for the
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A monarch, finally joining the French Resistance as its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, someone who rules a country.

clue.text: War is in conflict with Lionel Blair's vision?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a vision like Blair's, so the question mark flags a loose fit

indicators.note: in conflict suggests the words war and Lionel clashing and being jumbled together

explanation.surface: The entertainer Lionel Blair's view seems at odds with war.
explanation.walkthrough: Lionel Blair was a British TV entertainer, but the Blair meant is Eric Blair, whose pen name was George Orwell; the adjective from his name describes his dystopian vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Blair wrote as George Orwell, so his dystopian vision is described with the adjective formed from his pen name.

clue.text: Young animal devouring last of fresh fish

indicators.note: devouring means the young animal swallows the next letter inside it

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, lion or fox

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of fresh

explanation.surface: A bear cub gobbling up the remains of a freshly caught fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Mischievous types slobbing around beneath government department

indicators.note: beneath places the shuffled letters below the department in this down light

parts.note: HO is the Home Office, a UK government department

indicators.note: around here means the letters of slobbing are moved about

explanation.surface: Idle troublemakers lounging about under a civil service department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a placement word but here it signals the anagram; 'beneath' does the placing, under HO in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobgoblins are impish, mischievous sprites of folklore.

clue.text: Supporters on beach mobbing key players

indicators.note: on puts the supporters above the rest in this down light

parts.note: bras are undergarments that support

indicators.note: mobbing means the sands crowd round the key

parts.note: sands are a beach
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Fans on a beach swarming round important performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass bands are groups of musicians, so players fits as a plural noun.

clue.text: Spooner's agent cries out for associates

indicators.note: Spooner's means swapping the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent
bellows means shouts loudly

explanation.surface: A secret agent shouts the names of his accomplices.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of FED BELLOWS gives BED FELLOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfellows are people allied or linked together, as in strange bedfellows.

clue.text: Group of sailors standing back-to- back

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman; two of them stand here

indicators.note: standing back-to-back means the second sailor faces the opposite way to the first

explanation.surface: A crew of seamen standing back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors in the plural gives two ABs; the second is turned round so they stand back-to-back.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA was the Swedish pop group famous for Waterloo and Dancing Queen.

clue.text: For example, German tormenting sect in bed and breakfast?

indicators.note: tormenting suggests the letters of sect in bed being twisted

explanation.surface: A German harassing a religious sect at a guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict, poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, is a classic breakfast dish.

clue.text: Dismiss ecclesiastical reports as profane

indicators.note: reports signals that the answer is how the phrase dismiss ecclesiastical sounds when spoken

parts.note: to dismiss is to sack, and ecclesiastical means religious

explanation.surface: Getting rid of church reports because they are blasphemous.
explanation.walkthrough: This grid enters the word as printed, matching the sound pun; dictionaries spell it SACRILEGIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilegious means treating holy things with disrespect, which is what profane means.

clue.text: Scintillating parts of Gran Torino

parts.note: the Gran Torino is a Ford car; the parts of its engine that make sparks are what is wanted

explanation.surface: Brilliant moments in Clint Eastwood's film Gran Torino.
explanation.walkthrough: Gran Torino reads as the Clint Eastwood film, but it is the Ford car; scintillating literally means sparking.
explanation.definitionFit: Spark plugs ignite fuel in a car engine by producing an electric spark.

clue.text: A tenor isn't terribly sonorous

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of a tenor isn't being badly mangled

explanation.surface: A tenor whose voice is far from resonant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means extremely loud and powerful, after Stentor, the herald with a voice of fifty men.

clue.text: Team, reportedly on dope, given lesson in medley

indicators.note: on puts the team piece after the dope piece

parts.note: dope is slang for cannabis, also called pot
team sounds like teem, and to teem is to pour with rain
RI is religious instruction, a school lesson

explanation.surface: A sports team, rumoured to be on drugs, sent to a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' works on team: it sounds like teem, which gives POUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixture or miscellany of things, just as a medley is.

clue.text: Very strong boxer almost slipped circling ring

indicators.note: almost means the boxer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Rocky is the boxer of the Sylvester Stallone films

indicators.note: circling means the slipped piece goes around the ring

parts.note: slid means slipped
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A tough boxer nearly lost his footing going round the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means utterly firm and dependable, as strong as rock.

clue.text: Part of Cleopatra's lascivious, gyrating dance

indicators.note: gyrating means the concealed letters spin round to read backwards
part of means the answer lies within the words Cleopatra's lascivious

explanation.surface: Cleopatra performing a sensual, swirling dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Period preceding a mass in oratory

definitions.meaning: the time leading up to an event
spoken aloud, a mass is amass

explanation.surface: The time before a church service in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Oratory looks like a chapel, but 'in oratory' means as spoken: A MASS said aloud is AMASS, which RUN UP means.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up to an election is the preceding period; running up debts means accumulating them.

clue.text: Sentenced fraud; heartless fellow caught in act

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: caught in means the shortened fellow sits inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the fellow is removed

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A swindler, a callous man caught in the act, was sentenced.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemned means handed a punishment by a court, typically a death sentence.

clue.text: Diggers parking by lake initially startled animals

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign symbol for parking
lough is the Irish word for a lake

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of startled

parts.note: hares are animals

explanation.surface: Excavators in a car park near a lake scared some animals.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUGH is the Irish lake word, like the Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughshares are the blades of ploughs that cut into the soil, so they dig.

clue.text: It may lead to matrimony

parts.note: a bride is led down the church passageway to the altar to be married

explanation.surface: Something like an engagement that may end in marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courtship; the thing that literally leads to the wedding is the church passage the bride walks down.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle of a church is the walkway leading to the altar where couples marry.

clue.text: Add runs to draw level

indicators.note: add means the runs piece is attached to the draw piece

parts.note: a tie is a draw
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Score a few more runs to draw the match level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or layer, as in tiers of seats.

clue.text: Celebrity essentially posed on pitch

indicators.note: essentially takes the central letter, the essence, of posed

parts.note: tar and pitch are both black sticky substances

explanation.surface: A famous person modelling on the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous person, a celebrity.

clue.text: College student's final module

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: final takes the last letter of student's

explanation.surface: A university student's last course module.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a component part of a course, which is what a module is.

clue.text: Court accepts girl is touring Cuba with international scholar

indicators.note: accepts means the court takes everything else inside it

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: touring means is goes around the next letters

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: A tribunal admits a young woman who travels in Cuba with a global academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A classicist is an expert in ancient Greek and Latin, a kind of scholar.

clue.text: Half the characters in prison confess to crime

indicators.note: half the characters in means only half the letters of the prison's name are kept

parts.note: the prison is the famous maximum-security jail at Ossining, New York, whose name is one word said twice

explanation.surface: Half the inmates in a jail admit to an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison is SING SING in New York State; half its letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is underworld slang for informing or confessing to the police.

clue.text: Endure a TV broadcast about Right being opportunist

indicators.note: about means the scattered letters wrap round the next piece
broadcast suggests the letters of endure a TV being scattered

explanation.surface: Putting up with a television programme about a right-wing chancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the anagram of ENDURE A TV, which wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is someone who seeks fortune by risky or unscrupulous means, an opportunist.
